title: Unit Testing Examples
description: Small Unit Testing examples from the lessons. Each example links back to its explanation and practice task.

examples.title: One small behaviour
examples.description: A unit is a small piece of behaviour, often a function. Test what it returns for a clear input.

examples.title: Arrange act assert
examples.description: Arrange prepares input. Act runs the code. Assert checks the result. These three steps make a test easy to read.
examples.code:
const input = 3; // arrange
const actual = input * input; // act
console.log(actual === 9); // assert

examples.title: Name the rule
examples.description: A useful test name says the rule and the situation. Someone should understand a failure without opening every line of code.

examples.title: Compare values carefully
examples.description: Equality checks need to match the data you care about. Two different objects are not the same object even if their fields match.

examples.title: Boundary cases in a unit
examples.description: Choose a value where a rule changes. Test both sides so a wrong comparison sign is visible.
examples.code:
const passes = score => score >= 5;
console.log(passes(4) === false, passes(5) === true);

examples.title: Test expected errors
examples.description: Some functions should reject bad input. Check that the rejection happens and that its message is useful.

examples.title: Fresh data for each test
examples.description: Tests should not depend on the order they run. Make fresh input when a function changes its input.

examples.title: Inject a dependency
examples.description: A dependency is another function or object that code uses. Passing it in lets a test choose a simple, predictable replacement.
examples.code:
function greetFrom(getName) { return "Hi " + getName(); }
console.log(greetFrom(() => "Asha") === "Hi Asha");

examples.title: Spies record calls
examples.description: A spy records how a dependency was used. This helps test actions such as saving a message.

examples.title: Wait for async work
examples.description: Async work finishes later. A test must wait for its promise before checking the result.
examples.code:
async function getScore() { return 8; }
getScore().then(score => console.log(score === 8));

examples.title: Use several cases
examples.description: A table of cases checks the same rule with several inputs. Keep each expected result easy to see.
examples.code:
const cases = [[0, 0], [2, 4], [-3, -6]];
for (const [input, expected] of cases) console.log(input * 2 === expected);

examples.title: Read a failure before fixing it
examples.description: A failure is evidence that actual and expected results differ. Check the requirement before changing either the code or the expected answer.
